clue.text: Position in the saddle had to be acceptable

definitions.meaning: a rider rising off the seat in the stirrups takes this upright stance
an argument or claim that holds good under scrutiny is said to do this

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both a rider rising in the stirrups and a claim that survives testing.

clue.text: Ribbon displayed by special troops on horseback, at first

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service, Britain's special forces regiment

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word horseback

explanation.surface: Elite soldiers on horses show off a decorative ribbon.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a broad ribbon or band worn across the body or round the waist.

clue.text: Decline a prize

parts.note: a trophy is a prize

explanation.definitionFit: Atrophy is wasting away, a gradual decline in strength or function.

clue.text: Day taken up meeting a new Indian finance minister

indicators.note: in a down clue taken up means written upwards, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: Wed is the abbreviation for Wednesday, a day

explanation.surface: A day is fixed for meeting the newly appointed Indian finance minister.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'taken up' means read from the bottom, so the day's abbreviation comes out backwards. A dewan was an official in Mughal and princely India.
explanation.definitionFit: A dewan was a chief minister or finance officer of an Indian state under Mughal and princely rule.

clue.text: What Eurosceptics are to put forward

definitions.meaning: opponents of the euro are in favour of keeping sterling, read as pro and pound
to propose a theory or idea for consideration

explanation.walkthrough: Eurosceptics are British opponents of the EU; many wanted to keep the pound rather than adopt the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: To propound a theory is to put it forward for others to consider.

clue.text: Fitting description' of the pet one trained

indicators.note: something trained is shaped and put into new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A suitable label is found for a pet that has been through obedience school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges THEPET with I (one) to give the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive name or phrase aptly attached to someone, like a nickname.

clue.text: Regenerating leaderless London borough

indicators.note: leaderless means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: healing means regenerating, as tissue does

explanation.surface: A London district is being redeveloped without anyone in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaderless' drops the H from HEALING. Ealing is a borough in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Ealing is one of the boroughs of west London, famous for its film studios.

clue.text: Demand more input for processing

indicators.note: processing works material over into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A computer user demands further data to be processed.
explanation.definitionFit: To importune is to pester someone with persistent demands.

clue.text: Suspend boxer appearing dejected

parts.note: to hang something is to suspend it
a boxer is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A fighter looks miserable after being given a suspension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' reads as a fighter but is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is shamefaced and dejected.

clue.text: A welcome shower falling in New York

definitions.text: A welcome shower falling in New York

parts.words: A welcome shower falling in New York
parts.note: sounds like rain after drought, but the shower is of paper strips thrown down on parading heroes in Manhattan

explanation.definitionFit: New York greets returning heroes with parades where strips of paper rain from office windows.

clue.text: Survey showing growth's about to cut off at a certain point

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for the growths is read backwards

parts.note: a wart is a small growth on the skin; growth's stands for growth is, giving the plural sense warts

parts.words: to cut off at a certain point
parts.note: to poll a tree or horn is to cut off its top

explanation.surface: An investigation into how fast something grows, with a plan to trim it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growth's' looks like a possessive but is a plural, and 'about' signals the turnaround; to poll a tree is to lop its top.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw poll is an informal survey taken to gauge opinion quickly.

clue.text: Word-play I construed originally in an ancient language

parts.note: a pun is play on words

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word construed

explanation.surface: A scholar interprets a bit of punning in an old tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Punic was the Semitic language of ancient Carthage.

clue.text: Card games for a channel crossing

parts.note: pontoon is a card game, the British name for twenty-one
bridge is another card game, played by partnerships

explanation.surface: Card-playing helps pass the time on a ferry over the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: PONTOON is the British name for the card game also called blackjack or twenty-one.
explanation.definitionFit: A pontoon bridge is a temporary bridge on floating supports, used to get across a waterway.

clue.text: Simple diet possibly prescribed for the fast

indicators.note: possibly says these letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A doctor might recommend plain food to a patient who is fasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges SIMPLEDIET. 'Fast' looks like going without food but means speeding drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal maximum speed is imposed on fast drivers, so it is a rule set for them.

clue.text: Money upfront required here for a ring

definitions.text: Money upfront required here for a ring

parts.words: Money upfront required here for a ring
parts.note: reads like a jeweller demanding cash for a wedding ring, but the ring is a telephone call paid for in advance at a coin-operated box

explanation.definitionFit: A public telephone took coins before a call, so money came first for a ring.

clue.text: Buffoonery in Equus

definitions.meaning: Peter Shaffer's drama about a boy who blinds horses

explanation.walkthrough: Equus is a 1973 stage play by Peter Shaffer centred on horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means rough fooling, and split in two it describes a play about horses.

clue.text: Rod's going back to fetch valuable piece of information

indicators.note: going back means the word for the rod is read in reverse

parts.note: rod is slang, chiefly American, for a gun
to fetch is to get

explanation.surface: Someone named Rod returns to collect an important tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a man's name but is old gangster slang for a pistol, and 'going back' turns that word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a small but valuable item, as in a nugget of wisdom or information.

clue.text: Poisonous shrub replacing an old elder

indicators.note: replacing is read as re-placing, putting the letters in new positions

explanation.surface: A toxic bush is planted where an aged elder tree once stood.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleander is an evergreen shrub whose every part is highly toxic.

clue.text: Call for more in Continental centre

parts.note: en is the French word for in
the core is the centre

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the middle of Europe an audience demands another song.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting the French word asks performers to come back for another piece.

clue.text: Headed a second short uprising in fortress

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads the whole run from bottom to top

parts.note: led means headed

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: Someone led a brief revolt inside a stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims TICK to TIC; 'uprising' turns LEDATIC round to give the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress guarding a city.

clue.text: Depressed about hip requiring a certain investment

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling depressed
c, short for circa, means about
taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient feeling low about a hip operation thinks of their stock portfolio.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-chip shares are those of solid, reliable companies, regarded as safe investments.

clue.text: Tribesman almost clashed with drunk being noisy

annotationWithheld.why: Tribesman almost clashed with drunk being noisy (7): HIT + a homophone of TIGHT (drunk, 'being noisy') gives the answer, but no reading accounts for 'almost'
annotationWithheld.clue: Tribesman almost clashed with drunk being noisy

clue.text: Post Office admits rise in fees is artificial

indicators.note: admits means the abbreviation lets the other piece in
in a down clue a rise reads the word upwards, so it is reversed

parts.note: dues are fees

explanation.surface: The Post Office lets in a fee increase that is bogus.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rise' means the fees word is read upwards; 'admits' then lets it in between the two letters for Post Office.
explanation.definitionFit: Pseudo means sham or false, not genuine.

clue.text: They've given one the right open mail first

indicators.note: first says the word for mail comes ahead of the word for open

parts.note: letters are mail
patent means open or plain to see

explanation.surface: The right to read others' post is granted: open the mail first.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters patent are open documents from a sovereign granting a right, title or monopoly.

clue.text: Cardinal king put upon made a mistake

indicators.note: in a down clue put upon means placed on top of the other piece

parts.note: ER, Edwardus Rex, was the cipher of King Edward
cardinal is a deep red colour, after cardinals' robes

explanation.surface: A churchman and a monarch are imposed upon, and something went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: ER usually means the Queen, but it equally stands for Edward Rex, a king.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, so the past form means made one.

clue.text: Meal consisting of hash

definitions.meaning: a dish or serving of food
a muddle, as in making a hash of things

explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old term for a portion of food and also a muddle.

clue.text: Sitter needing a dummy

definitions.meaning: one who sits for an artist or photographer

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person posing for an artist and a tailor's mannequin.

clue.text: Reinforce the Tube?

definitions.meaning: to emphasise or stress a point
the Tube is London's underground railway, read whimsically as a line that runs under the ground

explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's underground railway; the question mark flags the playful reading of the answer as an under line.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to draw a line under it; the Tube is jokingly a line beneath the city.

clue.text: Verbal warning to watch out for the quarry

definitions.text: Verbal warning to watch out for the quarry

parts.words: Verbal warning to watch out for the quarry
parts.note: sounds like a shout to beware of a stone pit, but the quarry is the hunted fox and the cry is the one huntsmen give on sighting it

explanation.walkthrough: In British fox hunting, riders shout this cry when the fox is seen.
explanation.definitionFit: The huntsman's shout announces that the hunted animal has been spotted.

clue.text: Pay for remedy

definitions.meaning: to make amends or compensation for a wrong
a means of setting a wrong right

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means compensating for a wrong; as a noun it means the remedy itself.
